clue.text: Still without a proposal?

parts.note: a motion is a proposal put before a meeting
-less is the suffix meaning without

explanation.surface: A suitor wonders whether he is still unengaged, no proposal yet made.
explanation.definitionFit: Something still is unmoving, entirely at rest.

clue.text: Transom opened to reveal moon

indicators.note: the letters are revealed inside the words transom opened, running across the join

explanation.surface: Opening a window above a door lets someone see the moon.
explanation.definitionFit: To moon about is to mooch listlessly, which is to sulk idly.

clue.text: Cost of ring

explanation.surface: What it costs to make a phone call.
explanation.definitionFit: A toll is a charge for using a road or bridge, and to toll is to ring a bell slowly.

clue.text: Being practised, made cocktail

parts.note: an old hand is experienced, so old means practised
fashioned means made or shaped

explanation.surface: A skilled barman has produced a cocktail.
explanation.definitionFit: An Old Fashioned is a classic whisky cocktail with bitters and sugar.

clue.text: Landowner set about trespasser at last

indicators.note: set goes about, around, the letter taken from trespasser

parts.note: to lay is to set down, so set gives laid

indicators.note: at last picks the final letter of trespasser

explanation.surface: A landowner finally sets upon a trespasser.
explanation.walkthrough: LAIRD is the Scottish word for a landed proprietor.
explanation.definitionFit: A laird is a Scottish estate owner.

clue.text: Tender lamb, say, and mint

parts.note: sweet can mean gentle or tender
lamb is an example of meat, the say marking an example

explanation.surface: Tender lamb served with mint sauce, a culinary picture.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pairs lamb with mint sauce; mint is in fact the definition, a mint being a sweet.
explanation.definitionFit: A mint is a confection, and sweetmeat is an old word for a sweet or candy.

clue.text: One resented being at work to get a crust

explanation.surface: A strikebreaker crosses the picket line to earn a living.
explanation.definitionFit: A scab is a worker resented for breaking a strike, and also the dry crust over a healing wound.

clue.text: Stain on character the best people wholly lack according to Yeats

definitions.text: the best people wholly lack according to Yeats

explanation.surface: A literary reflection on blemished reputations and Yeats's view of the best.
explanation.walkthrough: Yeats's poem The Second Coming says: 'The best lack all conviction, while the worst are full of passionate intensity'.
explanation.definitionFit: A criminal record blots a reputation, and Yeats's line names firm belief as what the best lack.

clue.text: Carry beds from riotous scene

parts.note: to bear is to carry
flower beds make up a garden

explanation.surface: Someone carries flowerbeds away from a disorderly scene.
explanation.definitionFit: A bear garden was a place for bear-baiting, hence any rowdy, chaotic place.

clue.text: Loaded water for use on building site

parts.note: piled means heaped up, loaded
a river is a body of water

explanation.surface: Loaded water carried to a construction site.
explanation.definitionFit: A pile driver is a machine hammering piles into the ground during construction.

clue.text: I can put forward name of old American

indicators.note: the letter named by name is shifted to an earlier place in the words I can

parts.note: taken as written, giving four letters

explanation.surface: Someone offers to suggest the name of a historical American.
explanation.walkthrough: N is the standard abbreviation for name; moving it forward in ICAN gives INCA.
explanation.definitionFit: The Incas were the pre-Columbian people of Peru, natives of the Americas long ago.

clue.text: Work up posh name in snobbish rivalry

indicators.note: to work something is to knead it into a new form, so these letters are reshaped

explanation.surface: Someone works up a grand name to compete socially.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Work' rearranges UPPOSHNAME plus IN, the 'in' that looks like a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the art of always outdoing others to gain a social edge.

clue.text: Difficult to get permanent place to park

parts.note: hard means difficult
standing means permanent, as in a standing army

explanation.surface: Finding a permanent parking spot is tough.
explanation.walkthrough: Hardstanding is British for a hard-surfaced area where vehicles may be parked.
explanation.definitionFit: Hardstanding is a paved surface for parking vehicles or aircraft.

clue.text: Cursorily wash part of body that's over basin

parts.note: to splash yourself is to wash hastily
the back is part of the body

explanation.surface: Someone gives part of their body a quick wash.
explanation.definitionFit: A splashback is the panel behind a sink protecting the wall from splashes.

clue.text: Paid seller outrageously for footwear

indicators.note: outrageously suggests wild disorder, so the letters of paid seller are thrown about

explanation.surface: Someone overpaid a vendor for shoes.
explanation.definitionFit: An espadrille is a canvas shoe with a rope sole.

clue.text: Quickly pass to the resolution

indicators.note: a resolution breaks something into parts and resolves them anew, so pass to the is rearranged

explanation.surface: Instructions to move a matter swiftly to a resolution.
explanation.definitionFit: Post-haste means with great speed, from the urgent posting of mail.

clue.text: Hoist 17 by stages

parts.note: 17 across is utter, which as an adjective means sheer
legs are stages of a journey or race

explanation.surface: A lifting device raised progressively.
explanation.walkthrough: The cross-reference 17 must be read via its answer: utter as an adjective, total.
explanation.definitionFit: Sheerlegs are a lifting apparatus of two or more spars lashed together, a kind of crane.

clue.text: Articulate — don't start to talk indistinctly

indicators.note: the opening letter of the word for talking indistinctly is dropped

parts.note: to mutter is to speak unclearly

explanation.surface: A command to speak clearly, not mumble.
explanation.definitionFit: To articulate is to express in words, to say aloud.

clue.text: It was in Texas, but in the style of Missouri

parts.note: a la is French for in the style of
MO is the postal abbreviation for Missouri

explanation.surface: A historical place in Texas, yet styled like Missouri.
explanation.walkthrough: The Alamo is the mission in San Antonio, Texas, famous for its 1836 siege.
explanation.definitionFit: The Alamo is a fort in Texas besieged in 1836.

clue.text: Unrehearsed way for Snug to play a lion?

definitions.text: way for Snug to play a lion?

explanation.surface: Advice to an amateur actor on playing a lion.
explanation.walkthrough: In A Midsummer Night's Dream Snug the joiner plays the Lion, and Quince tells him he may do it extempore, for it is nothing but roaring.
explanation.definitionFit: Extempore means improvised, and Quince tells Snug to roar the Lion off the cuff.

clue.text: Arab doing business by shrewd bargaining

parts.note: an Arab is a breed of horse
trading means doing business

explanation.surface: An Arab merchant does business through hard bargaining.
explanation.definitionFit: Horse-trading is hard-nosed negotiating, from the haggling of horse dealers.

clue.text: B. I hear, for Bertie Wooster

explanation.surface: A note on how Bertie Wooster might be described, heard as a letter.
explanation.walkthrough: The letter B sounds like bee, and a drone is a male bee; Bertie Wooster belongs to P.G. Wodehouse's Drones Club.
explanation.definitionFit: A male bee is a drone, and Wodehouse's idle young men are members of the Drones Club.

clue.text: No one wounded in memorial

parts.note: no one is nil, nought, shaped like the letter O
bit is an old past participle of bite, so wounded by teeth

explanation.surface: Nobody was hurt at a memorial ceremony.
explanation.definitionFit: An obit is an obituary, a tribute marking someone's death.

clue.text: Quick-tempered, bur grow easy in the end

parts.note: to wax is to grow, as the moon does

indicators.note: in the end selects the final letter of easy

explanation.surface: Someone irritable, but who calms down eventually.
explanation.walkthrough: The page prints 'bur' for 'but', a misprint for the link word. Waxy is British slang for angry.
explanation.definitionFit: Waxy is old British slang for angry or irritable.

clue.text: The French follow, say, across the bar

indicators.note: the French word follows the other piece

parts.note: read as a cross: a gives A, and X is a cross, say
le is French for the

explanation.surface: French people follow over the bar.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'across' as 'a cross': A plus X, which is an example (say) of a cross.
explanation.definitionFit: An axle is the bar or rod on which wheels turn.

clue.text: Phone-box out of order? I answer with strange apprehension

indicators.note: a broken phone-box is out of order, and the letters of phone-box are put out of order

explanation.surface: Finding a phone-box broken, someone answers with odd anxiety.
explanation.definitionFit: Xenophobia is fear of foreigners, an apprehension about what is strange.

clue.text: King finds shelter for artist

parts.note: K is the chess abbreviation for king
the lee is the sheltered side

explanation.surface: A monarch gives refuge to a painter.
explanation.definitionFit: Paul Klee was a Swiss-German painter.

clue.text: Possible alternative to the op, say

definitions.text: Possible alternative to the op, say

indicators.note: a possible alternative arrangement of letters, so to the op say is reshuffled

explanation.surface: Suggesting a treatment other than surgery.
explanation.definitionFit: Osteopathy is a manipulative therapy offered as an option instead of surgery.
